scenes.text: In part one, we saw how diffusion turns noise into a picture. [1] But AI can now make videos too, and even edit your photos with just a sentence. [2] So in part two, let's see how.

A video is just many images in a row, so why is it so much harder? [1] An image only needs to look good once. [2] But a video needs every frame to match the next, the same face, the same shirt, and motion that makes physical sense.

right.title: A video
right.label: hundreds of frames that must match

scenes.text: Here's how video models handle it. [1] You describe a scene, like rain falling on a Hyderabad street at night. [2] The model treats the whole clip as one block of frames, across space and time. [3] It starts with noise, for every frame at once, [4] and cleans them all up together, so they stay consistent, [5] giving you a short clip, usually a few seconds long.

data.heading: How AI makes video
nodes: “Rain on a Hyderabad street at night”

scenes.text: AI can also edit the images you already have. [1] Inpainting, where you select an area, and the AI redraws just that part. [2] Outpainting, where it extends the picture beyond its edges. [3] And instruction editing, where you simply say, make it sunset, and it changes the scene for you.

Want better results? Build your image prompt like this. [1] A lazy prompt, like a cat, gives you something generic. [2] Now add a subject with details, a fluffy orange cat wearing a tiny helmet. [3] Then the setting, riding a scooter through a busy Hyderabad market. [4] The style, colourful 3D animation. [5] And the camera, low angle, golden hour light. [6] And now, it looks like a movie poster.

Riding a scooter through a busy Hyderabad market.
data.goodReply: A vivid, cinematic scene: an orange cat in a helmet zooming through a golden-hour market.

scenes.text: So where do people use this? [1] Short video ads and social media clips. [2] Film and game previews, before anything is shot. [3] And quick photo fixes, like removing people from the background.

Here's a common myth. [1] People think AI can already make a full movie from one prompt. [2] Not yet. Most models make short clips, and keeping characters consistent across scenes is still hard. Real productions stitch many clips together, with a lot of human editing.

data.myth: AI can already make a full movie from one prompt.
data.fact: Most models make short clips. Real productions stitch many clips with lots of human editing.
